subject: Synthesis of today's discovery — deployment targets, SLOs, next technical steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amit Patel <amit.patel@lodepay.com>, Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@lodepay.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Synthesis of today's discovery — deployment targets, SLOs, next technical steps

Hi Amit / Sara —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick synthesis from my side so we have a shared record and clear next steps. I focused this on the constraints and outcomes we discussed so your engineering team and ours can align on feasibility.

Top pain points you confirmed:
- High variance in 95th/99th latency during peak billing-window (5–8x baseline).
- Token cost sensitivity: top-line model spend is projected to double under current traffic if we don't optimize batching/caching.
- Regulatory requirement: all PCI-adjacent logs must be retained for 90 days; you'll need private tenancy for any PII processing.

Goals / success criteria we captured:
- 95th percentile latency <= 450ms for single-turn inference at 2k RPS sustained (regional US-east).
- Cost target: reduce per-100k-token spend by >=30% vs current LLM provider via batching + quantized model variants.
- Deployment: private VPC with dedicated pool for checkout/authorization flows; hosted variants for lower-sensitivity features.

Model and workload notes:
- Primary model: LodePay will use a mixture of a 13B open model for production inference and smaller 3B for non-critical enrichment. Peak sequence length ~1024 tokens (mostly invoice parsing + short chat).
- KV cache reuse is expected to help because many user sessions re-use prefixes (payment templates). Estimated cache hit ~35% after warmup.

Topology sketch (high-level):
- Dedicated GPU pool (private) for auth/payment intents with aggressive latency routing.
- Hosted fallback pool (lower-cost) for enrichment and background tasks.
- Cross-region failover configured for east/west to tolerate AZ-level incidents.

Attachments: I'm sharing a first-pass SLO matrix and a rough topology sketch (attached). Please confirm assumptions below and flag anything I missed.

Assumptions to confirm from your side:
1) Peak sustained RPS: 2k (confirmed by Sara on call) — please attach any observed traffic traces if different.
2) Critical paths: authorization and charge creation are the only PCI-adjacent flows that must remain in private tenancy.
3) Security: LodePay will require SOC2 + customer-managed KMS for private deployment.

Proposed next steps (we discussed these live):
- Rishi / Jasmine to run an internal topology fit and sizing based on the SLOs and model sizes (I'm asking for a prioritized ops playbook). Target: 48h for first sizing.
- LodePay to share anonymized traffic trace and a short list of 10 representative prompts for our quality/latency tests.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive (1h) next week with LodePay's infra and security leads to finalize KMS / network requirements.

If that matches what you heard, reply with OK and any clarifications and we'll kick off the sizing run.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Synthesis of today's discovery — deployment targets, SLOs, next technical steps

Vanessa — thanks for the clear summary, this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirming peak sustained RPS: 2k during billing-window (we saw short spikes to 4k for ~10m windows). I'll attach a 24h sample trace.
- PCI-adjacent flows: yes, only tokenization/authorization flows need private tenancy. We can run enrichment (e.g., customer notes enrichment) in hosted.
- KMS: we will use AWS KMS CMKs; we want Redwood to support BYOK and key rotation policies.

Two asks before the deep-dive: 
1) Can you include warm vs cold KV-cache behavior in your sizing (we saw 35% hit after ~24h, but cold-starts double latency)?
2) If you propose quantized model variants, can you provide a short A/B plan that preserves accuracy within 1.5% of the baseline?

OK to proceed with the sizing run. Sara and I are available Tue/Wed 10–12 PT next week for the technical deep-dive.

—Amit
Amit Patel
Head of Platform Engineering | LodePay
amit.patel@lodepay.com

Subject: RE: Synthesis of today's discovery — deployment targets, SLOs, next technical steps

Vanessa / Jasmine —

I ran a quick sanity pass on the SLOs you outlined. Initial notes before we do a proper sizing run: 

1) Latency target (95th <= 450ms at 2k RPS) — achievable but depends on:
   - batching policy (we should use dynamic batching with a 25–50ms aggregation window in the dedicated pool).
   - KV cache: cold-starts will push the 95th into the 600–800ms range unless we pre-warm on day-0. Suggest a pre-warm strategy for the first 24h and a traffic ramp.

2) GPU sizing: for the 13B quantized variant (4-bit), expect ~3–4x throughput improvement vs fp16 and ~2x lower memory. For 2k sustained RPS at 1024 sequence length, initial cluster of 8x A100-40GB equiv (dedicated) with continuous batching looks right; we'll sanity-check with perf curves.

3) Fallback / routing: recommend a routing policy that pins PCI flows to the private pool and routes enrichment to hosted with automatic model-variant fallback if private pool saturates.

I'll put together a short doc with perf assumptions and two sizing options (conservative / optimized) and attach perf curves for the quantized 13B. ETA: EOD tomorrow (Tue).

- rishi
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
